# Repo sessions (server): SessionProvisioner, SessionManager, /api/sessions, /api/repos, limit, close flow, ownership

## What to build

The server side of **repo sessions** in graph-manager (`apps/graph-manager`). A user opens a terminal by choosing a repository, a branch and an agent: `POST /api/sessions` acquires a `WorkspaceHost` from a `SessionProvisioner`, calls `host.prepare` (clone or reuse, check out the branch), and opens a terminal in it. A repository with at least one open terminal is a live session; a second terminal on the same repository joins that session. `GM_MAX_SESSIONS` caps the sessions per user (409 with an exact message). Closing the last terminal of a session ends it: a clean clone ends at once; a clone with uncommitted changes asks (push / keep / discard). Ending waits while a run of the session is live, then releases the session. Every `/api/sessions/:id/*`, `/api/terminals/:id/*` and `/api/runs/:ws/*` route answers 404 when the session, terminal or workspace does not belong to `req.user`, and `AppContext.hostFor` becomes session-aware. Also `GET /api/repos` (forge search for the New terminal dialog) and `GET /api/repos/branches`.

This task is **server only**: no React changes (the dialog, sidebar and close dialog are a later task). `packages/graph-execution` (the engine) must not change at all. Project sessions (`{ projectId }`) are a later task: answer 400 for them here.

## Before you start: what dependency tasks already built

Read these first; they exist in the codebase now. Names below follow the shared contract; if a detail in the code differs (a parameter name, an import path), follow the code and keep the behaviour described here.

- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/identity.ts`: `export interface User { id: string; name: string; email?: string }`, `ADMIN_USER`, and `req.user: User` set by the auth hook on every authenticated request.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts`: `interface Store { instance(): InstanceData; forUser(user: User): Promise<UserStore> }`, `interface UserStore { get(): Data; update(fn: (d: Data) => void): Promise<void>; reviewers(): Reviewer[] }`, `SqlStore`, and the zod `dataSchema` (per-user `Data`). Routes do `const us = await ctx.store.forUser(req.user)`. `UserStore.update` runs updates one at a time per user, like the old `DataStore.update` (lines 179–197 of the old file): a throw inside `fn` aborts that update.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/db/` (`Db` with `query/exec/transaction`) and `apps/graph-manager/src/server/accounts.ts` (`createUser`, `findUserByUsername`, `getUser`, `countUsers`, ... all taking a `Db`). Find how `app.ts` exposes the `Db` on `AppContext` (e.g. `ctx.db`) and how tests log in as a second user (look in `src/server/test-helpers.ts` and `src/server/accounts.test.ts` for a helper; otherwise `createUser(db, …)` then `POST /api/auth/login { username, password }`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/host/types.ts`: `RepoRef = { forge: "github" | "gitlab"; owner: string; name: string; baseUrl?: string }`, `PtyProcess`, `EngineStart`, and `WorkspaceHost` with `prepare`, `spawnPty`, `startEngine`, `readFile`, `listFiles`, `listRuns`, `runDetail`, `git`, `activity`, `changes`, `save`, `discard`, `loginFiles`, `pushBranch`:
  ```ts
  prepare(p: { repo: RepoRef; branch: { new: string } | { existing: string } }): Promise<{ workspaceId: string; branch: string }>;
  listRuns(workspaceId: string): Promise<RunSummary[]>;
  changes(workspaceId: string): Promise<string[]>;            // git status --porcelain lines, empty when clean
  save(p: { workspaceId: string; branch: string; message: string }): Promise<{ pushed: boolean; skipped: string[]; error?: string }>;
  discard(workspaceId: string): Promise<void>;                 // git reset --hard + git clean -fd, ignored files kept
  ```
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/host/local.ts`: `LocalWorkspaceHost` (the one shared local host; `prepare` clones into the workspaces folder or fetches and checks out, and answers 409 `{"error":"acme/api has uncommitted changes. Close its session with Push or Discard first."}` when the clone is dirty and the branch differs). `apps/graph-manager/src/server/host/contract.ts`: `hostContractSuite(name, makeHost)`.
- `AppContext.hostFor(workspaceId, user): Promise<WorkspaceHost>` in `app.ts` (today it returns the local host for everything). Routes `specs.ts`, `inspect.ts`, `runs.ts`, `resume.ts`, `pr.ts`, `terminals.ts` call it.
- `terminals.ts`: `TerminalManager` now spawns through a `WorkspaceHost` (`host.spawnPty`) instead of calling `pty.spawn` directly (old lines 261–277). Read the current `create` signature before changing it.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `docs/prd/hosted-sessions.md` — sections "Session lifecycle" (state diagram), "Decisions" rows on sessions, limit, ask-before-closing, secret skipping, branch default, and "Requirements → Sessions" and "SessionProvisioner". Source of truth.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/app.ts` (lines 39–54 `AppContext`, 56–70 `BuildAppOptions`, 80–102 context creation, 125–137 hooks, 145–159 route registration, 106–123 error handler: an `Error` with `statusCode` 4xx is answered as `{ error: message }`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.ts` (whole file, 159 lines) — `POST /api/terminals` agent launch (lines 65–103: `getAgent`, `isInstalled`, `prepareProjectConfig`, `adapter.launch`, `commandLine(launch.argv) + "\r"`), `DELETE /api/terminals/:id` (106–109), the WebSocket (129–158).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/terminals.ts` (lines 8–43 `TerminalInfo`/`CreateTerminal`, 73–95 `Term`, 233–259 `create`, 338–345 `list`/`get`, 392–400 `remove`, 418–435 `info`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/forges.ts` (lines 5–35 `ForgeRepo`/`ForgeClient`, 50–55 `gitAuthArgs`, 57–59 `redact`, 207–232 `forgeClient`/`connFor`/`clientFor`) and `routes/forges.ts` (lines 73–77 `GET /api/forges/:kind/repos`). After the store change `connFor`/`clientFor` read the user's own forge tokens; check their current signature.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/runs.ts` (lines 24–49 `RunSummary`; a run is still running while `kind === "live"`, see `stillRunning` lines 247–255 and `summarize` 257–272).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.ts` (lines 102–110 `GET /api/runs`, 112–119 `GET /api/runs/:ws/:runId`), `routes/pr.ts` (`/api/runs/:ws/:runId/pr`), `routes/resume.ts` (`/api/runs/:ws/:runId/resume`, `/api/runs/:ws/:runId/sandbox/stop`), `routes/specs.ts` and `routes/inspect.ts` and `routes/sandbox.ts` (`/api/workspaces/:id/...`), `routes/workspaces.ts` (`GET /api/workspaces`), `proxy.ts` (line ~84: the run-page proxy resolves `/runs/:ws/:runId/view`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/runhome.ts` (lines 8, 31–39): ids starting with `project~` are projects (already per user through the user's store).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts` (lines 8–24 `Config`, 95–106 `envSchema`, 109–128 `loadConfig`) and `config.test.ts`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/test-helpers.ts` (`tempDir`, `testConfig`, `appWithLogin`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/workspaces.test.ts` (lines 1–47) — how tests start the fake forge (`startFakeForge` from `apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-forge.mjs`; GitHub repo `octo/hello`, token `gh-good`; GitLab `grp/sub/proj`, token `gl-good`, base URL `${forge.url}/gitlab`) and connect it with `PUT /api/forges/github`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.test.ts` (lines 1–80) — WebSocket and inject patterns; terminal tests are `describe.skipIf(process.platform === "win32")`.

## Patterns to follow

**Errors with a status** (handled by the error handler in `app.ts` lines 116–119):
```ts
class HttpError extends Error { constructor(readonly statusCode: number, message: string) { super(message); } }
throw new HttpError(409, `You have ${max} open repositories. Close all terminals of one to open another.`);
```

**Body parsing** (mirror `routes/terminals.ts` lines 11–21): zod `.strict()` objects; a `ZodError` becomes 400 `{ error: "<path>: <message>" }` automatically.

**Store writes**: always `const us = await ctx.store.forUser(user); await us.update((d) => { ... })`. Never keep a reference to `us.get()` across an `await`; re-read after.

**Forge auth for git over HTTPS** (`forges.ts` lines 50–55): `git ${gitAuthArgs(kind, token).join(" ")} ls-remote …` — never put a token into a URL or an error message (`redact`).

**Tests**: vitest, `app.inject` with the login cookie, fake forge for git remotes, temp dirs from `tempDir()`; never real tokens or the network.

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: add `GM_MAX_SESSIONS` to `envSchema` (optional integer ≥ 1, same `optional.pipe(z.coerce.number…)` style as `GM_PORT` on line 96) and `maxSessions?: number` to `Config`, set in `loadConfig` only when given. Add, do not rewrite: sibling tasks add their own variables to the same schema.
- **VALIDATE**: `config.test.ts`: `GM_MAX_SESSIONS=3` → `maxSessions: 3`; unset → undefined; `0` and `x` → `ConfigError`.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sessions/provisioner.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** exactly:
  ```ts
  export interface SessionProvisioner {
    /** A session container for one repository or one project. Must be idempotent per sessionId (graph-manager calls it again after a restart). */
    acquire(p: { user: User; sessionId: string }): Promise<WorkspaceHost>;
    release(p: { user: User; sessionId: string }): Promise<void>;
    /** A run container for a sandboxed run (hosted only). */
    acquireRun(p: { user: User; sessionId: string; runId: string }): Promise<WorkspaceHost>;
    releaseRun(p: { user: User; runId: string }): Promise<void>;
  }
  export class LocalProvisioner implements SessionProvisioner {
    constructor(private readonly host: WorkspaceHost) {}
    async acquire() { return this.host; }   // the one shared LocalWorkspaceHost
    async release() {}                       // the clone stays on disk
    async acquireRun(): Promise<WorkspaceHost> { throw new Error("LocalProvisioner has no run containers: local sandboxed runs use Docker"); }
    async releaseRun() {}
  }
  ```
- **IMPORTS**: `User` from `../identity.js`, `WorkspaceHost` from `../host/types.js`.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sessions/secrets.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `isSecretPath(rel: string): boolean` — true when the basename is `.env`, starts with `.env.`, ends with `.pem` or `.key`, or starts with `id_rsa` (so `id_rsa`, `id_rsa.pub`). `parsePorcelainZ(out: string): string[]` parsing `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` (entries `XY path\0`; for renames/copies `R`/`C` the next NUL field is the old path, skip it). `selectSaveFiles(paths: string[]): { add: string[]; skipped: string[] }`.
- **VALIDATE**: unit test `sessions/secrets.test.ts` with `.env`, `config/.env.local`, `certs/a.pem`, `a.key`, `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `id_rsa.pub` skipped and `src/env.ts`, `.envrc`, `README.md` kept; a rename entry parsed correctly.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/host/local.ts` (`LocalWorkspaceHost.save`)

- **IMPLEMENT**: make `save` stage only allowed files and list what it skipped. If task 5's `save` already does exactly this, keep it and only add the tests below. Otherwise:
  1. `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` → `parsePorcelainZ` → `selectSaveFiles`.
  2. Also skip files git ignores: pipe `add` into `git check-ignore --no-index -z --stdin`; matches move to `skipped` (untracked ignored files never show in status anyway).
  3. If `add` is not empty: `git add -A -- <paths>` (chunks of 100), then `git commit -m <message>`; when `git config user.email` is empty, pass `-c user.name=graph-manager -c user.email=graph-manager@localhost`.
  4. `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>`, authenticated the same way task 5's `prepare` authenticates clone/fetch (reuse it; if `prepare` gets the forge token from an option, do the same for save — you may add an optional field to `save`'s parameter object, keeping the spec's fields).
  5. Return `{ pushed: true, skipped }`, or on a failed push `{ pushed: false, skipped, error: <git's last stderr line, token redacted> }`. Never throw for a failed push.
- **GOTCHA**: `.graph-execution/` is in the clone's `.git/info/exclude`, so run folders are never staged. Keep `discard` as task 5 wrote it (`git reset --hard` + `git clean -fd`, ignored files kept).
- **VALIDATE**: add to the host contract tests or a `host/local.save.test.ts`: in a clone of a temp bare repo (`git init --bare`), write `a.txt`, `.env`, `k.pem`, and a git-ignored `build/x`; `save` pushes a commit to the bare repo's branch containing only `a.txt` and returns `skipped` containing `.env` and `k.pem`; with the remote URL changed to a missing path, `save` returns `pushed: false` with an `error`.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** (add to `dataSchema`, do not rewrite it; other tasks add fields too):
  ```ts
  export const repoRefSchema = z.object({ forge: z.enum(["github", "gitlab"]), owner: z.string(), name: z.string(), baseUrl: z.string().optional() });
  export const sessionSchema = z.object({
    id: z.string(), repo: repoRefSchema, workspaceId: z.string(), branch: z.string(),
    state: z.enum(["starting", "live", "asking", "ending", "save-failed"]),
    startedAt: z.string(), error: z.string().optional(),
  });
  // in dataSchema:
  sessions: z.record(z.string(), sessionSchema).default({}),
  /** Workspace ids this user has opened a session on (kept after the session ends, so its runs stay visible). */
  ownedWorkspaces: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
  ```
  Export `type SessionRecord = z.infer<typeof sessionSchema>`.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/terminals.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: add `userId?: string` and `sessionId?: string` to `CreateTerminal`, `Term` and `TerminalInfo` (copied in `create`, returned by `info()` only when set, like `workspaceId` on line 425). Add `listFor(userId: string): TerminalInfo[]` and `ofSession(sessionId: string): TerminalInfo[]`.
- **GOTCHA**: keep `restart`, `rename`, `attach` unchanged; they work by id.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - Extract the "spawn a shell or an agent" part of `POST /api/terminals` (lines 65–103) into an exported `openTerminal(ctx, user, p: { host: WorkspaceHost; workspaceId?: string; cwd: string; agent?: AgentId; title?: string; cols?: number; rows?: number; sessionId?: string; env?: Record<string, string> }): Promise<TerminalInfo & { connected?: PrepareResult }>`. It throws `HttpError(400, "<binary> is not installed")` like today. It sets `userId: user.id` and `sessionId`. Keep the agent's `env`, `input` and title rule (`${adapter.label} · ${repo}`). `POST /api/terminals` uses it too and keeps its current behaviour (its `workspaceId` must pass the ownership check below, else 404 `workspace not found`).
  - `GET /api/terminals` → `{ terminals: terminals.listFor(req.user.id) }`.
  - `DELETE /api/terminals/:id`, `POST /api/terminals/:id/restart`, `PATCH /api/terminals/:id` and the WebSocket `/api/terminals/:id/ws`: when the terminal's `userId` is not `req.user.id`, answer exactly like an unknown terminal (404 `{"error":"terminal not found"}`; the WebSocket closes with `4404`).
  - `DELETE /api/terminals/:id`: after `terminals.remove`, if the terminal had a `sessionId` and `terminals.ofSession(sessionId)` is now empty, call `ctx.sessions.lastTerminalClosed(req.user, sessionId)`. If it returns `{ ask }` answer **200** `{ sessionId, ask: { changes: string[] } }`; otherwise 204 as today.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sessions/sessions.ts` (`SessionManager`)

- **IMPLEMENT** a class constructed with `{ store: Store; provisioner: SessionProvisioner; terminals: TerminalManager; openTerminal: (user, p) => Promise<TerminalInfo>; localHost: WorkspaceHost; maxSessions?: number; pollMs?: number (default 5000); liveRuns?: (host: WorkspaceHost, workspaceId: string) => Promise<number>; countUsers: () => Promise<number>; log?: (msg: string, err?: unknown) => void }`. Default `liveRuns` = `(await host.listRuns(wsId)).filter((r) => r.kind === "live").length`. Public API (later tasks — the idle loop and agent logins — call these; keep the names):
  - `open(user, body): Promise<{ sessionId: string; terminalId: string; branch: string }>`
  - `openTerminal(user, sessionId, p: { agent?; cols?; rows?; title? }): Promise<TerminalInfo>` — 404 unless the session is the user's; 409 `{"error":"session is <state>"}` unless `live` or `asking` (an `asking` session goes back to `live`).
  - `list(user): Promise<SessionView[]>` where `SessionView = SessionRecord & { terminals: string[] }` (ids of the user's terminals with that `sessionId`).
  - `get(user, id): Promise<SessionRecord | undefined>`
  - `lastTerminalClosed(user, id): Promise<{ ask?: { changes: string[] } }>`
  - `close(user, id, action: "push" | "keep" | "discard"): Promise<{ session: SessionView; skipped?: string[] }>`
  - `closeSession(user, id)`: removes all its terminals then behaves like `lastTerminalClosed` (used by `DELETE /api/sessions/:id`).
  - `end(user, id): Promise<void>` — idempotent per id (one pending end per session).
  - `setState(user, id, state, error?)`, `hostOf(user, session): Promise<WorkspaceHost>` (cached `Map<sessionId, WorkspaceHost>`; on a miss calls `provisioner.acquire` again), `liveRuns(user, session): Promise<number>`, `terminalIds(user, id): string[]`, `lastActiveAt(id): Date` (in memory: set at open, at every state change and when a terminal closes; falls back to `startedAt`), `all(): Array<{ user: User; session: SessionRecord }>` (every known session of every user, from an in-memory index kept in sync with the stores), `addHooks(h: SessionHooks)`, `settled(): Promise<void>` (resolves when no `end` is pending; for tests), `restore(): Promise<void>`, `ownsWorkspace(user, workspaceId): Promise<boolean>`, `hostFor(user, workspaceId): Promise<WorkspaceHost>`.
  - `export interface SessionHooks { afterPrepare?(p: { user: User; session: SessionRecord; host: WorkspaceHost }): Promise<void>; beforeRelease?(p: { user: User; session: SessionRecord; host: WorkspaceHost }): Promise<void>; terminalEnv?(user: User): Promise<Record<string, string>> }`. Run every registered hook in order; a hook error is logged and does not stop the flow. `terminalEnv` results are merged into the `env` of every session terminal.
- **`open` flow** (`body` = `{ repo: RepoRef; branch?: { new?: string } | { existing: string }; agent?; cols?; rows?; title? }`):
  1. Look for the user's session with the same repo (`forge`, `owner`, `name` equal). `live` or `asking` → set `live`, open a terminal in it, return `{ sessionId, terminalId, branch: session.branch }` (the requested branch is ignored). `starting` → 409 `{"error":"<owner>/<name> is still opening. Try again in a moment."}`. `ending` or `save-failed` → 409 `{"error":"<owner>/<name> is closing. Try again when it has closed."}`.
  2. Inside one `us.update`: count the user's sessions in **any** state; if `maxSessions` is set and the count is `>= maxSessions`, throw `HttpError(409, \`You have ${maxSessions} open repositories. Close all terminals of one to open another.\`)`; else insert `{ id, repo, workspaceId: "", branch: <requested>, state: "starting", startedAt }`. Ids: `randomBytes(6).toString("hex")`.
  3. Branch: `{ existing: name }` as given; `{ new: name }` as given; `{ new }` without a name or no `branch` → `gm/<user-id>-<yyyymmdd>-<4 random [a-z0-9]>` with the user id reduced to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` (others become `-`). Reject a name that fails `git check-ref-format --branch` rules (`..`, leading `-` or `/`, trailing `/` or `.lock`, spaces, `~^:?*[\`) with 400 `{"error":"branch: invalid branch name"}`.
  4. `host = await provisioner.acquire({ user, sessionId })`, then `host.prepare({ repo, branch })`. On any error: delete the record, `provisioner.release`, rethrow (a 409 from `prepare`, like the dirty-clone message, reaches the client unchanged).
  5. Run `afterPrepare` hooks; set `workspaceId`, `branch` (as returned), `state: "live"`; add the workspace id to `ownedWorkspaces` (no duplicates).
  6. Open the terminal with `openTerminal(user, { host, workspaceId, cwd: <as task 5's terminal creation needs it>, agent, cols, rows, title, sessionId, env })`. If that fails (e.g. agent not installed), the session stays `live` with no terminals (it can be closed with `DELETE /api/sessions/:id`) and the error is returned.
- **`lastTerminalClosed`**: only for a `live` session. `changes = await host.changes(workspaceId)`; empty → `ending` and start `end` (not awaited); else `asking` and return `{ ask: { changes } }`.
- **`close`**: `keep` only from `asking` → `live`. `push` from `asking` or `save-failed` → state `ending`, `host.save({ workspaceId, branch: session.branch, message: \`graph-manager: save session ${id}\` })`; `pushed: false` → `save-failed` with `error` (no release; return the view with state `save-failed` and `skipped`), else start `end` and return `skipped`. `discard` from `asking` or `save-failed` → `host.discard(workspaceId)` → start `end`. Any other state/action → 409 `{"error":"session is <state>"}`. Unknown or foreign id → 404 `{"error":"session not found"}`.
- **`end`**: state `ending`; loop: `while (await liveRuns(...) > 0) await sleep(pollMs)`; then `beforeRelease` hooks, `provisioner.release({ user, sessionId })`, drop the cached host, delete the record (keep `ownedWorkspaces`). A failing `release` keeps the record in `ending` with `error` set and is logged.
- **`restore`** (called once from `app.ts` in an `onReady` hook): for every user row (`SELECT id FROM users` through the `Db`, then `getUser`), load the store: `starting` records are deleted (they never finished), `ending` records resume `end`, others stay. When `countUsers()` is 1, add every existing clone (`listWorkspaces(config.workspacesDir)` from `workspaces.ts`) to that user's `ownedWorkspaces`, so an upgraded single-user install keeps its run history once a second account appears.
- **`ownsWorkspace(user, id)`**: true for ids starting with `project~` (projects are already per user); true when `countUsers() <= 1` (an install with one account behaves as today); else true when the user has a session with that `workspaceId` or `ownedWorkspaces` contains it.
- **`hostFor(user, workspaceId)`**: not owned → throw `HttpError(404, "unknown workspace")`; the user's session on that workspace in a non-`starting` state → `hostOf(user, session)`; else `localHost`.
- **IMPORTS**: `randomBytes` from `node:crypto`; `User` from `../identity.js`; `Store`, `SessionRecord` from `../store.js`; `WorkspaceHost`, `RepoRef` from `../host/types.js`; `TerminalManager`, `TerminalInfo` from `../terminals.js`; `listWorkspaces` from `../workspaces.js`.
- **GOTCHA**: never hold the cached `Data` across awaits; always re-read `us.get().sessions[id]` after an await (another request may have changed it). Timers must be `unref()`'d and stopped on `app.close()` (`app.addHook("onClose", …)`), or vitest hangs.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/sessions.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** `export async function sessionRoutes(app, ctx)`:
  - `GET /api/sessions` → `{ sessions: SessionView[], limit: number | null }` (`limit` = `config.maxSessions ?? null`; the UI shows "2 of 3 repositories open").
  - `POST /api/sessions` body (zod, strict): `{ repo?: { forge: "github" | "gitlab"; owner: string (min 1); name: string (min 1); baseUrl?: string }, projectId?: string, branch?: { new?: string } | { existing: string }, agent?: z.enum(AGENT_IDS), cols?, rows? (int 2–1000), title? }`. Exactly one of `repo`/`projectId`, else 400 `{"error":"pass repo or projectId"}`. `projectId` → 400 `{"error":"project sessions are not supported yet"}` (a later task implements them). For a GitLab repo without `baseUrl`, use the user's saved GitLab base URL. → **201** `{ sessionId, terminalId, branch }`.
  - `POST /api/sessions/:id/terminals` `{ agent?, cols?, rows?, title? }` → 201 the `TerminalInfo`.
  - `POST /api/sessions/:id/close` `{ action: "push" | "keep" | "discard" }` → 200 `{ session, skipped? }`.
  - `DELETE /api/sessions/:id` → same answers as `DELETE /api/terminals/:id` for the last terminal (200 `{ sessionId, ask }` or 204).
  - `GET /api/repos?q=` → for each connected forge of the user, `listRepos(q)` (from `forges.ts`); map each `ForgeRepo` to `{ repo: RepoRef, fullPath, defaultBranch, private, webUrl, live: boolean, sessionId?: string, branch?: string }` (`owner` = `fullPath` without its last segment — GitLab groups may nest, e.g. `grp/sub`; `name` = last segment; `baseUrl` = the saved GitLab base URL for GitLab). Repos with a session of the user come first with `live: true`, its `sessionId` and `branch`. Answer `{ repos, forges: { github: boolean, gitlab: boolean } }`. No forge connected → `{ repos: [], forges: { github: false, gitlab: false } }`. A forge error bubbles as `ForgeError` (the error handler maps it).
  - `GET /api/repos/branches?forge=&owner=&name=` → `{ defaultBranch, branches: string[] }` from `getRepo(fullPath)` then `git <gitAuthArgs> ls-remote --heads -- <cloneUrl>` (execa, `reject: false`; strip `refs/heads/`; default branch first, the rest sorted). ## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `POST /api/sessions { repo: { forge: "github", owner: "octo", name: "hello" }, branch: { new: "feat-x" } }` → 201 `{ sessionId, terminalId, branch: "feat-x" }`; the clone exists on branch `feat-x`; `GET /api/sessions` lists it `live` with that terminal id.
- [ ] Without a branch name the branch matches `^gm/admin-\d{8}-[a-z0-9]{4}$` (for user `admin`).
- [ ] A second `POST /api/sessions` on the same repo (any branch) → 201 with the same `sessionId` and the first branch; the session has 2 terminals.
- [ ] With `GM_MAX_SESSIONS=1` (`testConfig(dir, { maxSessions: 1 })`) and one session, a session on another repo → 409 `{"error":"You have 1 open repositories. Close all terminals of one to open another."}` (the number is the limit, text unchanged).
- [ ] Deleting the last terminal of a clean clone → 204; after `sessions.settled()` the session is gone and a new repo can be opened under the limit.
- [ ] With an uncommitted file, deleting the last terminal → 200 `{ sessionId, ask: { changes: [...] } }`, state `asking`, still counts toward the limit. `close { action: "keep" }` → `live`; `push` → the bare repo's branch has a commit `graph-manager: save session <id>` without `.env`/`*.pem`, `skipped` lists them, session released; `discard` → clone clean, session released.
- [ ] A failed push → state `save-failed` with `error`; `close push` retries; `close discard` drops the changes and releases.
- [ ] While `liveRuns` reports 1, a closed session stays `ending`; when it reports 0 it is released.
- [ ] Opening an existing clone on a different branch while it is dirty → 409 `{"error":"octo/hello has uncommitted changes. Close its session with Push or Discard first."}` (from `prepare`).
- [ ] A second account gets 404 for the first account's `/api/sessions/:id/close`, `/api/sessions/:id/terminals`, `DELETE /api/terminals/:id`, `PATCH /api/terminals/:id`, `/api/runs/github~octo~hello/x`, does not see the session or terminal in its lists, and its WebSocket to the terminal closes with 4404.
- [ ] `GET /api/repos?q=hel` lists `octo/hello` as `{ repo: { forge: "github", owner: "octo", name: "hello" }, … }`, `live: true` first when it has a session; GitLab `grp/sub/proj` maps to `owner: "grp/sub"`. `GET /api/repos/branches?forge=github&owner=octo&name=hello` → `{ defaultBranch: "main", branches: ["main", …] }`.
- [ ] `POST /api/sessions { projectId: "x" }` → 400; neither `repo` nor `projectId` → 400.
- [ ] `packages/graph-execution` is unchanged; `npm run typecheck && npm run lint` pass.
